brief.headline: Offer to pay in 15 days (freeing ₹26.60 L cash for us) in exchange for a 5–6% price cut — their cash is stuck for 101 days so they'll value speed, and we're still in the fair market band.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 5–6% price cut to stay comfortably inside the fair market band
priceAsk.target: Around ₹235–240/kg — our current price sits at the top of the fair band (₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg), so there's room to come down while staying market-fair
priceAsk.basis: The market ask for pharma/ORS sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), verdict: MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band). A 5–6% cut keeps us well inside that band and reflects the faster payment we're offering.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt — offer this as the trade for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹26.60 L cash for us by paying 15 days faster

brief.financialLeverage: They're a ₹1064.86 Cr converter but only keep 2.3% of every ₹100 they sell, so profit is tight. Their cash is stuck for 101 days — much longer than similar firms (64d) — which means they need cash quickly. They borrow money at about 12.16%, so paying them 15 days early is worth roughly 0.5% to them. We're only 0.61% of their revenue, so we're tiny to them — but their 'grey zone' distress score (2.36) and EPF payment delays mean they can't afford to lose any customer. Push firmly on price-for-speed, but don't squeeze so hard you tip a fragile supplier.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than peers
They borrow at a high rate, so early payment has real value to them
They're in the grey distress zone
We're a tiny customer to them
Their profit is thin, so a deep price cut could hurt supply
They already take longer to pay their own suppliers than peers

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film and conversion — can second-source laminate sachets at scale (already a qualified converter)

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, does pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source fit (revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health D 31/100, so verify stability first)

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier — proven and scalable for laminate sachets

risks: They're in the grey distress zone (2.36 Altman Z) and have EPF payment delays — don't push so hard on price that you tip them into real trouble and lose supply
Profit is only 2.3% — a big price cut eats most of that, so tie the cut tightly to the 15-day payment (which saves them 12.16% borrowing cost on that cash)
We're 0.61% of their revenue — we have almost no volume leverage, so the ask must rest on the payment-speed trade and the market price band, not on threatening to walk
Credit rating is CARE BBB+ / Stable — middling; keep Huhtamaki or UFLEX warm as a backup in case their financial stress worsens
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to 15-day payment to help your cash flow — in return, we need you to bring the laminate price down 5–6% to the middle of the market's fair band.
